USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Prior macrolide exposure

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with H. pylori infection has previously received several courses of clarithromycin. Susceptibility results are unavailable. Why is empiric reuse of a clarithromycin-based triple regimen a concern in this setting?

  1. The PPI becomes an antibiotic after prior macrolide use
  2. Resistance can be excluded merely because pain is mild
  3. Macrolide resistance can substantially reduce eradication success
  4. Clarithromycin has no antibacterial activity against any organism
  5. Previous exposure guarantees lifelong allergy
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Macrolide resistance can substantially reduce eradication success

Prior exposure and resistance concerns affect regimen selection; clarithromycin therapy should be susceptibility guided.

Understanding the options

Macrolide resistance can substantially reduce eradication success
Prior exposure and resistance concerns affect regimen selection; clarithromycin therapy should be susceptibility guided.
Clarithromycin has no antibacterial activity against any organism
It is an antibiotic, but resistance limits its use here.
Previous exposure guarantees lifelong allergy
Exposure does not itself establish allergy.
The PPI becomes an antibiotic after prior macrolide use
Acid suppression does not become antimicrobial therapy in that way.
Resistance can be excluded merely because pain is mild
Symptom severity does not determine susceptibility.
